cfg.extra_body_bad_body: Nothing was saved. extra_body rides as-is in the request, so broken JSON would be a setting that looks applied and does nothing:
cfg.extra_body_not_object: must be a JSON object, not a list or a number
cfg.h.API.api_key: Key for the main endpoint. Leave it empty for a local server that asks for none — llama.cpp, vLLM and Ollama do not.
cfg.h.API.extra_body:
PASSTHROUGH: this JSON rides AS-IS in the body of every request to this endpoint. For what is not standardised and is not ours to translate: qwen wants {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true}}, deepseek wants {"reasoning_effort": "high"}, and both answer in reasoning_content.

It must be a JSON object. It does NOT inherit: each model carries its own (sending enable_thinking to a model that never heard of it is a 400). It cannot override messages, model, tools or stream; anything else (temperature, max_tokens, top_p…) it can, and it wins.

Bad JSON is NOT saved silently: you are told on save.
cfg.h.API.model: The model that drives the conversation. Its latency multiplies by every iteration of the agentic loop, so here fast beats clever: leave the slow and sharp one for planner_model and qa_model.
cfg.h.APP.log_tools_to_notes: Log every action the agent takes into the cmd_log note category: an audit trail of what it actually did on your machine. Ring-buffered at 300 and never indexed, so it costs you nothing in searches.
cfg.h.BROWSER.fallback_model: Pool alias ([MODEL:x]) that rescues a step when the main model fails, instead of burning retries.
cfg.h.BROWSER.flash_mode: Skips the agent's evaluation/thinking so the model emits ONLY the action JSON. Fixes most 'Invalid JSON' failures with local models. auto = on.
cfg.h.BROWSER.headless: Browse without showing the browser window
cfg.h.BROWSER.max_steps_default: Steps the browsing agent may take before giving up. Each step is a page action plus an LLM call: this is what stops a site that never loads from burning your afternoon.
cfg.h.BROWSER.model: Which pool model DRIVES the browser (browser-use). By default the conversation's: the one the tab has pinned or, if none, the base. One that sees (vision) works best.
cfg.h.BROWSER.structured_output: force = the LLM server constrains the output with response_format/json_schema (llama.cpp, llama-swap, vLLM) so invalid JSON is impossible — the cure for 'Invalid JSON: expected ident'. auto = legacy behaviour. off = never force.
cfg.h.BROWSER.use_thinking: Pass 'thinking' mode to the browsing agent. Only worth it on reasoning models (qwen3-thinking, deepseek-r1, QwQ); on the rest it just spends tokens.
cfg.h.BROWSER.use_vision: Whether the BROWSER sends screenshots to the model. 'auto' asks the config which is the point: this model's own [MODEL:X] vision if it declares one, otherwise [CHAT] vision. true/false forces it and overrules both.
cfg.h.BROWSER.user_agent: User-Agent the browser announces. Change it when a site serves you a degraded page or blocks you outright for looking automated.
cfg.h.CHAT.auto_route_models: Route each turn to a pool specialist automatically. Off = only manual /model.
cfg.h.CHAT.client_tool_timeout: Max seconds the MCP waits for a tool the GUI executes (plan_and_orchestrate runs the whole orchestration there). 900 is too short for local models.
cfg.h.CHAT.compact_keep_recent: Recent messages that are never compacted. Compaction summarises the old part of a conversation; these last ones stay verbatim, because that is where the thread of what you are doing lives.
cfg.h.CHAT.compact_threshold: Compact the context when it reaches this fraction of the window
cfg.h.CHAT.context_length: Context window in tokens. 0 = auto-detect from the server. Set it if your endpoint lies about it.
cfg.h.CHAT.council_gate_timeout: Seconds a council waits for your decision when the vote comes back split. Generous on purpose: you may be away. On timeout it STOPS and hands you the answer with the disagreement signed — which is never wrong, whereas spending another round nobody asked for is.
cfg.h.CHAT.council_max_rounds: Ceiling on a council's rounds. It is NOT the policy: when the vote comes back without a unanimous placet the council ASKS you whether to spend another round, and never repeats on its own. This only stops a stuck loop from spinning if something keeps answering «again» with nobody there.
cfg.h.CHAT.escalate_model: WHO takes over: a pool alias, or `auto` to let the router pick by reading the profiles. «Bigger» is not in the data, so it is a decision, not a guess. Empty = auto.
cfg.h.CHAT.escalate_on_stall: When a turn stalls —two sterile nudges in a row, or the same call repeated until the loop breaks— it hands the turn ONCE to a stronger pool model instead of giving up. Said out loud (model_escalated event); never a silent swap. With no pool it does nothing rather than fake a hand-over.
cfg.h.CHAT.font_size: Base font size of the chat transcript (pixels, like the app stylesheet). Live zoom: Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0 / Ctrl+wheel — the zoomed value persists per machine and wins over this base.
cfg.h.CHAT.heavy_sterile_cut: Sterile streak that turns an EXPENSIVE tool (the browser) off for the rest of the turn: N results in a row empty/error/repeated, telling the model inside the result itself. Never by count of uses: if every navigation pays, let it run a hundred.
cfg.h.CHAT.max_tokens: Cap on the LLM's response length
cfg.h.CHAT.metacog: Metacognition: when the turn stalls (tools bringing nothing new, nothing crossed out on its intent list), the model is asked to stop and rethink the path. It asks, never dictates; at most twice per turn.
cfg.h.CHAT.metacog_stall_seconds: Seconds without real progress (with at least one sterile tool in between) before the tap. Checked between tools: it never interrupts one in flight — a long browse that brings data home never triggers it.
cfg.h.CHAT.metacog_stall_tools: Consecutive tools with nothing new (repeats, errors, empties) before the tap, however fast they are.
cfg.h.CHAT.multi_max_parallel: Sub-agents the orchestrator runs AT ONCE. Match it to your LLM server's slots: more than it can serve just queues them up and makes every one of them slower.
cfg.h.CHAT.multi_max_retries: Retries for a sub-task that fails or comes back empty, before the plan gives it up as failed. Whatever depends on it is then abandoned too, rather than left waiting.
cfg.h.CHAT.plan_ack_timeout: Seconds a plan waits for your approval before cancelling itself. Generous on purpose: you may be away. On timeout it CANCELS — better to lose the plan than to fan out to other people's machines with nobody watching.
cfg.h.CHAT.plan_approval: When to ask your permission before launching sub-agents. always (recommended) = ALWAYS, no plan runs behind your back · auto = only if it touches REMOTE nodes or exceeds plan_auto_limit sub-tasks · off = never. Scheduled (cron) turns never block: a local plan is auto-approved and one touching remote nodes is cancelled.
cfg.h.CHAT.plan_auto_limit: How many sub-tasks are auto-approved without asking, when plan_approval = auto. The gate trips when the plan EXCEEDS it: at 3, a 3-sub-task plan runs on its own and a 4-sub-task one asks. Set 1 to see almost every plan, or 0 to always be asked. A plan that touches other people's machines ALWAYS asks, whatever its size.
cfg.h.CHAT.plan_max_expansions: Ceiling on RE-SCALING rounds: how many times a running plan may grow because a sub-agent found the job bigger than assumed. 0 freezes it even if you tick the box. A plan that can grow needs a ceiling, or a bad day becomes a runaway.
cfg.h.CHAT.plan_max_subtasks: Hard ceiling of sub-tasks in one plan, counting whatever re-scaling adds. Reached, the sub-agents stop being asked for more: it is the difference between an ambitious plan and a runaway one.
cfg.h.CHAT.planner_model: Pool alias that runs the PLANNER and the synthesizer. They run once per turn, so judgement matters more than speed here (your big model). Empty = use the chat base.
cfg.h.CHAT.qa_budget_chars: How much evidence the reviewer may be shown. Past this it stops grading whether the claims match the sources and only judges the answer itself — reviewing against a fraction of the evidence calls real findings inventions. Raise it if qa_model has a big context.
cfg.h.CHAT.qa_max_rounds: How many times the reviewer may send an answer back before the turn is allowed to end anyway. Each round is a full retry: a stubborn critic must not be able to burn the whole budget arguing.
cfg.h.CHAT.qa_model: Pool alias that REVIEWS answers. Empty = the model that did the work reviews itself, and a small model judging itself approves. It runs once at the end: slow does not hurt here.
cfg.h.CHAT.history_transcript: The history keeps the turn's TRANSCRIPT as the model saw it (tool calls, results, reviewer notes, rejected drafts), not just question and answer. The context grows downward and the server's prefix cache serves from one turn to the next; with (question, answer) alone every turn re-processes the previous one cold. Turn off for the old, shorter, uncached shape.
cfg.h.CHAT.qa_review: When to review before accepting an answer: auto (only tool turns worth it) · always · off.
cfg.h.CHAT.session_inject_context: In a session with yourself from another machine, the agent works with your facts and lessons. Never in a session with a contact or a child: what they need goes as a skill or a pack
cfg.h.CHAT.subtask_timeout: Seconds the PLAN waits for ONE sub-task before going on without it. Not a clock on the work: a clock on the WAITING, which is the only thing that can hang for ever. The sub-task is marked failed and said out loud; its dependents fail honestly and the synthesis reports what never arrived. 0 = wait for ever: one stuck sub-agent freezes the whole plan.
cfg.h.CHAT.terminal_timeout: Max seconds for ONE command in the embedded terminal. A cut comes back as exit -1 with half the output, which reads like a failure and is not one: a deploy script, a pip install or a dnf all run well past a minute.
cfg.h.CHAT.timeout: Seconds to wait for the LLM on a single call. A reasoning model on slow hardware takes minutes: too low here and you get network errors that look like the model's fault.
cfg.h.CHAT.vision: Declares that your chat model CAN see images. It changes nothing on the server: it only stops the warning when you paste one. Tick it wrongly and the model will get an image it cannot read.
cfg.h.CRAWL4AI.magic: crawl4ai's ACTIVE anti-bot heuristics (they interact with the page: overlays, waits). They pass harder walls but can break some sites. Off by default: turn it on when a domain resists.
cfg.h.CRAWL4AI.max_depth: Prospective crawl depth: 0 = only the URL you give (default). 1-3 = follow links on the SAME domain up to that level.
cfg.h.CRAWL4AI.max_pages: Page cap when max_depth > 0, so a domain can't drag you through hundreds of pages.
cfg.h.CRAWL4AI.max_urls: How many URLs of one file /includeurls scrapes (0 = no limit). It is NOT crawl depth: each URL is fetched as a single page, links are not followed.
cfg.h.CRAWL4AI.override_navigator: Hides navigator.webdriver and friends in the scraper. Passive, on by default. It is the first thing anti-bot checks look at.
cfg.h.CRAWL4AI.simulate_user: Simulates user gestures (mouse, scroll) in the scraper. Active and intrusive: only for walls that demand 'life'. Off by default.
cfg.h.CRAWL4AI.stealth: Stealth patches for the scraper's browser (cascade step 1): hides automation fingerprints. Passive and cheap; without it, sites that detect bots bounce the scrape into the full-browser escalation (minutes).
cfg.h.CRAWL4AI.timeout: Seconds per page when scraping a URL
cfg.h.EXA.api_key: Key for Exa: a search engine built for retrieval, not for a human reading a page. It tends to bring back the passage that answers the question rather than the page that ranks for it.
cfg.h.EXA.limit: Maximum sources per search. Each arrives with its text, so raising it costs context, not just time.
cfg.h.EXA.max_chars: Characters kept per source. 0 = WHOLE, whatever the provider sent — if the tool returns 100k, that is the output. A cut here destroys the text before anything can hold it: not the spill store, not the RAG, not a later read_note. Size is handled downstream, where the original survives and every part of it is read.
cfg.h.EXA.mode: 'search' hands back RAW sources with their text and the agent synthesises them — it can quote, and the reviewer can check the quote. 'answer' has Exa write the answer with citations: fewer tokens and one hop, at the cost of judging somebody else's summary.
cfg.h.EXA.type: How it searches: 'auto' lets Exa decide (recommended), 'neural' searches by meaning, 'keyword' by words, 'fast' trades some quality for latency.
cfg.h.EXA.url: Exa endpoint. Change it only if the API moves — the point of having it here is not needing an editor that day.
cfg.h.FIRECRAWL.api_key: Key for Firecrawl. Unlike Perplexity it returns RAW sources: the agent reads and synthesises them itself, which is better when you want the material and not somebody's summary.
cfg.h.FIRECRAWL.limit: Maximum results per search. Each one arrives with its content, so raising it costs context, not just time.
cfg.h.FIRECRAWL.max_chars: Characters kept per source. 0 = whole, whatever the provider sent. Same as Exa's: a cut here loses the text for good.
cfg.h.FIRECRAWL.url: Firecrawl endpoint. Change it if you self-host it.
cfg.h.LESSONS.enabled: Extract lessons from what happens: the system distils what worked and what did not, and reuses it. Off, every conversation starts from zero experience.
cfg.h.LESSONS.extract_on_feedback: Distil a lesson the moment you rate an answer, instead of waiting for the background worker. Immediate, and one extra LLM call right there.
cfg.h.LESSONS.inject_on_chat: Put the relevant lessons into the chat's context. This is what makes the system stop repeating a mistake you already corrected once.
cfg.h.MCP.enabled: Whether to use the MCP at all. Off, the chat keeps working but with no tools, no memory and no multi-agent: it is just a plain LLM.
cfg.h.MCP.sync_every_min: How often, in minutes, to pull and push the encrypted snapshot while HOPLITA is open. Two machines open at once see each other without closing either. Pull first, push after: fetching before uploading is what stops you overwriting the other one's work. 0 = off, sync by hand.
cfg.h.MCP.sync_on_boot: On MCP start, pull your encrypted snapshot (chats, canvases, notes, facts, lessons, cron) so ANY face finds the machine up to date. The same for the GUI and the CLI. On for machines that are yours: it writes into your local database, so turn it off on any box you don't own — a headless child on someone else's server also starts an MCP. A config.ini older than this option stays off until you add the key.
cfg.h.MCP.url: Where the local MCP server listens
cfg.h.MODEL.context_length: This model's own context window, in tokens. Leave it at 'auto' and the real one is asked of its server on the first turn, which is right far more often than a number typed here. Write one only for an endpoint that lies about its window or does not expose it — and get it right: the meter and the automatic compaction both measure against this, so a wrong number makes every turn fold the conversation.
cfg.h.MODEL.vision: Does THIS pool model see images? Left as 'not declared' it falls back to [CHAT] vision, which is the normal case. Set it when one model of the pool differs from the rest — that is what stops a blind model being handed a screenshot when you pin it with /model.
cfg.h.MODEL.council: Does this model sit on councils? Unticked, it stays in the pool for everything else, but no council seats it: not on the council page, not when the model convenes one naming nobody, and naming it is refused. For a small model that adds nothing when examining or voting.
cfg.h.PERPLEXITY.api_key: Key for Perplexity. This provider answers already written and with citations, instead of handing back raw sources.
cfg.h.PERPLEXITY.model: Which Perplexity model searches (sonar, sonar-pro…). The bigger ones read more sources before writing.
cfg.h.PERPLEXITY.url: Perplexity endpoint. Only touch it to point at a proxy or a compatible gateway.
cfg.h.RAG.chunk_overlap: Words repeated between consecutive chunks, so an idea cut in half is not lost by whichever side of the cut it fell on.
cfg.h.RAG.chunk_size: Words per chunk when indexing. Small chunks retrieve precisely but lose the surrounding argument; big ones keep the reasoning but match anything.
cfg.h.RAG.max_chunk_chars: Character ceiling per chunk, so the embedding server's window is never exceeded. Tightened automatically on markup-heavy text, which tokenises far denser than prose.
cfg.h.RAG.min_similarity_score: Minimum similarity to accept a chunk (0-1)
cfg.h.RAG.search_k: How many fragments a RAG search brings back. More gives the model context; too many bury the good one under mediocre neighbours and eat the context window.
cfg.h.SEARCH.provider: Web search engine actually used: perplexity or firecrawl (the only two implemented).
cfg.h.SKILLS.ask_which: Before each turn, ask the model which of your skills is FOR this, showing it the index. Costs one short call. Off: only skills you pin with /skill pin go in.
cfg.h.TAVILY.api_key: Key for Tavily. It is the one provider that can return BOTH a written answer and the sources it used, so it returns both: the answer to read and the sources to check it against.
cfg.h.TAVILY.depth: 'basic' is one pass and is fast; 'advanced' digs more and costs more per search. Worth it for questions where the answer is not on the first page.
cfg.h.TAVILY.include_answer: Ask Tavily for a written answer on top of the sources. The sources come either way — this only adds the summary.
cfg.h.TAVILY.limit: Maximum sources per search. Each arrives with its content.
cfg.h.TAVILY.url: Tavily endpoint. Change it only if the API moves.
cfg.header_note: Change what you need and save (Ctrl+S): it applies in the app and reloads the MCP. [MCP_SERVERS] still needs an MCP restart. Only the values you touch are rewritten — your comments stay.
cfg.is_default: Not written in your config.ini — this is the app's default value. It is only saved if you change it.
cfg.mcpservers_note: One entry per external MCP server — as many as you want. Value: stdio:<command args> for a local process, or sse:https://url for a remote one. Extra keys named <entry>_something become env vars <ENTRY>_SOMETHING for that process (e.g. minimax_key). Changes here need an MCP restart.
cfg.models_note: Each line is a model HOPLITA can use: its name, which model it is and which server it runs on. ✎ opens its details, 🔌 checks that it answers.
cfg.pool_seeded: «{alias}» is the model you were using, written in the file's [API] section. It is here as a model now, and it is the base. Save to keep it.
cfg.others_note: Every remaining key found in your config.ini, grouped by section — nothing is hidden, including keys added in the future.
cfg.parse_error: config.ini can't be parsed ({err}). Only the raw text editor is available so nothing gets overwritten with empty values. Fix the error and reopen to get the forms back.
cfg.profile_hint: What it's good at, in plain language — the router reads this
cfg.reloaded_from_disk: ⚙ config.ini changed on disk — reloaded. Values that apply per turn (max iterations, timeouts) take effect on the NEXT one.
cfg.test_model_missing: «{model}» is NOT on the server (check the exact name)
cfg.tri_unset: not sure (uses «Models that do not say…» below)
cfg.usage_empty: No model has consumed tokens since the last reset.
cfg.usage_reset_confirm: Reset the meter? Every model's tally is cleared and the date is stamped, so «since when» always has an answer.
cfg.usage_since: Counting since {when}. It accumulates EVERYTHING that goes through the MCP (chat, council, planner, reviewer, distiller, weekly pass) plus the app's direct calls.
chat.agentic_tools_shelf: 🤖 Agent: {n} tools with schema + {shelf} on the shelf (fetched via load_tools) · max {max} iter
chat.clear_confirm_body:
{n} messages go, along with the fixed context (/fixed) and the open code project. There is no undo.

Sure?
chat.ctx_absurd: ⚠ [CHAT] context_length = {n} is not a context window (under {min} tokens). Ignoring it and detecting the real one from the server — with that value every turn compacted itself. Fix or remove the line in config.ini.
chat.ctx_alias_dead: ⚠ [{sec}] num_ctx is in your config.ini and is NO LONGER READ. There was one setting with two names; now there is one: rename it to context_length, or delete it and the real window is asked of the server.
chat.heavy_cut: ✂ {tool} sterile {n} times in a row — off for the rest of this turn (the source is not yielding the data this way)
chat.input_ph_code: Ask about this code — the answer appears in the conversation
chat.metacog_nudge: 🧭 No real progress ({tools} sterile tools) — metacognitive stop: rethinking the path…
chat.pool_note_header: AVAILABLE SPECIALIST MODELS. Besides you (the base model), there are other models you CAN delegate a task to if their profile fits the user's request better than you:
chat.pool_note_rule: When a task fits a specialist better than you (e.g. heavy coding with the code model), delegate it by calling plan_and_orchestrate with the task: the system will route it to the right model. If the user EXPLICITLY asks to use a specific model (e.g. 'use <model name>'), you MUST delegate to that model, not answer yourself.
chat.tab_more_tip: {n} more tabs that do not fit: pick one
chat.context_full: [⚠ CONTEXT FULL — the model could not write anything: the prompt is {pt} tokens and the completion was cut at once. Nothing to redo. Reset or compact this conversation, or open a new tab, and ask again.]
sess.autosave_failed: ⚠ This conversation could not be saved ({e}). After a restart it comes back as last saved.
chat.tab_rename_body: New name for this tab (and its saved session, if any):
chat.turn_echo_dead: ⚠ I have no valid answer: I kept repeating my internal record instead of addressing your message. Ask again or rephrase.
chat.turn_qa_capped: [⚠ UNVERIFIED: the reviewer rejected this answer and the redo budget ran out. Last objection: {why}]
chat.turn_qa_ok: ✓ the reviewer passed the final answer
chat.turn_trace_failed: ✗ the turn ended in error, with no answer: {e}
chat.turn_trace_more: (and {n} more step(s) that do not fit here)
child.add_intro: A specialised agent of yours that runs on this machine as a sub-agent. Say what it is for: what it knows, what it does, what it delivers, which of your notes or projects it works with. The model writes its pack (its role, the tools, folders and projects it needs) and then the pack opens for you to adjust.
child.add_desc_hint: e.g. Reviews the security of my PHP projects: looks for injections and leaked secrets, uses my notes in sec-notes, and reports each finding with its fix.
child.add_designing: The model is writing the child's pack; it opens when it is ready.
child.box_intro: A child of yours with its own identity on the server, that boots from a token with nothing typed in: in a docker or podman container on this machine, where whatever it runs, installs or breaks stays inside, or on any other machine with HOPLITA installed. Its token carries the model and, if you want, your web search, sealed so the server cannot read them.
child.box_key: API key, if it needs one
child.box_key_note: Every key in its kit is one the child holds and can spend, and anything it runs can read it. A key of its own with a spending cap is the safe choice.
child.box_search: Hand over my web search too
child.box_starting: Starting the child. The first time, the image is built first, which takes a few minutes; you'll get the result when it's done.
child.cap_code_tip: Read and analyse code: search, references, dependencies, lint.
child.cap_research_tip: Search notes, memory and documents, and read files.
child.cap_terminal_tip: Run commands. This gives it the whole toolbox.
child.cap_web_tip: Search, browse and scrape the internet.
child.cap_write_tip: Write notes and files. This gives it the whole toolbox.
child.capabilities: What it can do (which tools it gets)
child.caps_are_a_preset: A starting point: ticking them fills in the tools below, which are what counts. You can correct them afterwards.
child.edit_hint: Everything this child is. You can also just tell it in the chat (for instance, give it a folder or reinforce its role); that ADDS. Here you are looking at the whole thing, so what you save is what it becomes.
child.model_inherit: the same as the turn that calls it
child.projects: Task projects it works in — it can see their pending tasks, do them and update them. Nothing ticked = no restriction.
child.role: Role — what it is and how it works. This is what matters.
child.scope_hint: Note folders it can search, read and write. Nothing ticked = no restriction: it sees what you see. Its memory is always yours, whole — this only narrows the folders.
child.scope_no_folders: You have no note folders yet.
child.tools_hint: What this child may call. They come in families: the header tick turns a whole family on or off in one click, and says whether it is all, half or none. On top of that, search «delete», «pull» or whatever you like and use «enable / block what is shown». The general firewall still has the last word.
cmd.unknown: ❌ '/{cmd}' is not a command.{hint} Type /help to see them all.
code.binary_file: '{path}' looks binary; not opening it in the editor.
code.check_goal_hint: What you expect to see in the output, in words: no errors; pp512 above 2000…
code.check_goal_judged: The model judges the output against this when the run ends (and in the loop, before calling the work done).
code.check_goal_none: No goal: the verdict is the exit code alone.
code.check_goal_tip:
What the exit code CANNOT answer. a benchmark exits 0 whether it got faster or slower; a report exits 0 whether it found what it looked for or not.

Write it the way you would tell a person: «no errors in the log», «the figure above X», «faster than before». The run's output travels to the model and THE MODEL judges whether it holds; the verdict is exit 0 AND the judge saying yes, with its one-line why.

If nobody could judge it (no endpoint, unreadable answer), that is said as such and the verdict stays on the exit code: no green that means «I could not look», no invented red.

The agentic loop uses THE SAME judge: with a goal, «done» is exit 0 and the judge calling the bar met.
code.check_goal_unjudged: nobody could judge the goal «{expect}»: the verdict stays on the exit code
code.checkpoint_lost: ⚠ This session's restore points no longer exist in the repository (was it re-created?). Showing the plain diff.
code.clean_untracked: No changes to tracked files ({n} untracked).
code.close_project_hint: Leave code mode: the model stops seeing this project on every turn
code.closed_msg: Project closed. Back to normal mode.
code.commit_hint: What you did (becomes the commit message)

  gcc -Wall -Wextra -fsyntax-only *.c

Your account on the server is DELETED — for all your machines — and your federated children are revoked. Your contacts and links disappear and EVERYTHING stops syncing. Your shared notes, projects and calendar STAY local — nothing local is deleted, they just stop syncing.

help.commands:
📋 AVAILABLE COMMANDS  (/x — the old @command prefix still works as an alias)

— This tab's PINNED CONTEXT · rides WHOLE on EVERY turn, until you clear it —
/fixed <text>  →  Pin a permanent text (rules, data, contracts)
/include <file>  →  Pin the WHOLE file (200KB max, says when it cuts). Does NOT go to RAG.
   See what's pinned: 📌 /fixed button · Clear: tray → Clear fixed context

— SEARCHABLE KNOWLEDGE (RAG) · doesn't ride by itself: enters when you search it —
/addtext <file>  →  Load the file into RAG
/includeurl <url>  →  Download a URL into RAG
/includeurls <file>  →  Harvest the URLs from a file into RAG
/notes <category>  →  Dump a notes category into RAG
/searchrag <text>  →  Search RAG and ANSWER with the hits (the answer stays pinned)
/summary [topic]  →  Summarize what is LOADED in RAG (files, URLs, notes)

— CODE AND PROJECTS —
CODE tab (or /project in the CLI)  →  open a project: the model READS and edits
   the files itself (code_*, git checkpoints). No /include needed for code.
/verify <cmd>  →  DEFINITION OF DONE: the turn does not end until it exits 0
/goal <text>  →  The bar in words: the model reads it before starting and the reviewer uses it as the acceptance criterion

— THE TURN AND ITS JUDGES —
/model [name]  →  Pin this tab's model (no name = show the pool) · /model base returns
/qa [name|off|auto]  →  THIS tab's judge. /model qa <x> works too
/multi <task>  →  Plan a team of sub-agents and run them
/why  →  Which facts, lessons, rules and skills went into the model on the last turn, in full
/context  →  What the next prompt weighs, block by block, heaviest first
/compact  →  Fold the old part of this tab's context into a summary now
/queue  →  Messages waiting for the current turn · '/queue clear' empties it
/pin  →  Tie this tab to THIS machine: you see it from anywhere and its turns run here. /pin off unties · /pin ? says which

— SKILLS (reusable instructions injected into the prompt) —
/skill <search>  →  Find a skill and run it
/skill add <path.md>  →  Save a skill from a file (title = file name)
/skill add <name>: <text>  →  Save a skill written inline
/skill pin <search>  →  Keep it in context for the whole session
/skill pinned  →  List the pinned ones · /skill unpin <name> releases one

— UTILITIES —
/search <text>  →  Search online (the result gets indexed into RAG)
/todo <text>  →  Chat with the task/appointment manager (refreshes the TODO's saved URLs first)
/browse <instruction>  →  Autonomous browser (Playwright + LLM)
/alert <message>  →  Popup with sound (manual alert)
/creds  →  Credentials manager (encrypted user/password)
/help  →  This message

inject.escalated: [HANDED OVER — you are now {model}] The previous model stalled on this turn (same paths, no new data); its trace is above. Take a different approach and carry on.
inject.facts_header: [MEMORY — WHO THE USER IS: the lasting facts. What is ongoing in their life (projects, plans, recent matters) is NOT listed here: what matches this message comes in a block at the end, and when you are asked about or told of something you do not know, SEARCH before answering: recall(query, terms=[…]) for what may have come up in earlier conversations, and search_web for the rest. «I have no record» or «I am not aware of it» is not an answer. Never claim to have saved something you have not seen in these blocks or in recall. A fact is a short note; what was actually said is in the conversation it came from: when the detail matters (figures, names, what was decided), recall it from what was said instead of answering from the note. They are REFERENCE ONLY: do not repeat them and do not act on them unless they bear on what is being asked NOW. Use add_fact ONLY for NEW facts the user states in this message.] AND PRECEDENCE, which is sacred: what the user tells you NOW about their own life BEATS any fact in this list, always — a stored fact is an old photo, the owner is the source. If they say something that contradicts a fact, do not argue or ask them to confirm: update the memory with add_fact and move on — the memory itself recognises it as the same fact, an update or a newer truth, and retires the stale one. Each fact carries its id in brackets: that id is THE one edit_fact and delete_fact accept — never invent one.

inject.plan_gate: [HOPLITA] This reads like a plan and nothing of it was written to the project's memory. If it IS a plan: project_write('{cat}', note='future', text=<one line per pending item>) — and at most a couple of add_task for what starts NOW — then answer with a short summary saying so. If it is NOT a plan, reply exactly: {token}
inject.order:
🧭 ORDER OF WORK, ALWAYS THE SAME:
  1. DO I ALREADY HAVE THIS? Look at what is in front of you: the user's facts and the skills index. Do not search to find out whether something is saved — you can see it.
  2. IS THERE A SKILL THAT COVERS IT? Pull it with use_skill and FOLLOW IT. It exists because the generic answer was not good enough; a saved skill beats any search.
  3. ONLY THEN, tools or the web, carrying what you learned in 1 and 2 into the request.
Going to the internet with the answer already at home is the most expensive mistake you can make here.
inject.rules_header: [RULES THE USER GAVE YOU. They dictated them while correcting you. These are not suggestions: follow them. If you believe one does not apply to this case, say so out loud instead of quietly skipping it.]
inject.rules_truncated: [… and {n} more rule(s) that do not fit. Consolidate or delete them: you are keeping them for nothing.]
inject.skills_header: 📋 REFERENCE SKILLS — their FULL TEXT is right below: do NOT fetch them again with use_skill or load_tools. If none applies to THIS message, ignore them and move on:
inject.skills_index: 📋 YOUR SKILLS (titles and what they are for). If one covers what is being asked, pull it with use_skill("the title") and USE IT: it exists because the generic web answer was not good enough. Looking here comes BEFORE searching the web. {titles}

inject.spill_index: 🗄 THIS CONVERSATION'S WORKING MEMORY — large results you got as a digest, kept WHOLE here. The digest is an extract; the rest of each text is still searchable: search_working_memory(query='<any words, a name, a figure>') returns the passages that mention it, with the paragraphs around and their lines (title= narrows to one text, regex=true is grep), and read_note(category='working-memory', title=..., start_line, end_line) reads a span. prompts.compactor:
You are summarising the OLD part of a conversation so the model can keep working without it. This is a CONTRACT of what to preserve, in this order:
1. WHAT THE USER ASKED, every request, in their words where they matter; and what they DECIDED (options rejected included).
2. STATE: what is DONE, what is PENDING, what failed and why.
3. LITERAL IDENTIFIERS, copied verbatim, never paraphrased: paths, files, commands that worked, names, ids, URLs, numbers, versions, error messages.
4. WHAT THE TOOLS RETURNED AND STILL MATTERS, and where to reread it: keep the read_note(...) calls and other locators.
5. OPEN QUESTIONS and warnings (firewall, limits, permissions).
Drop chatter, superseded attempts and repetition. Third person, concise, in the conversation's language. Do NOT invent or fill in: what is not there is not there.
prompts.council_answer_user:
A council has been convened and you speak FIRST. Your answer is the one the others will examine.

THE MATTER:
{topic}

Answer it IN FULL: reasoned, concrete and complete, saying what each claim rests on. If the matter can be read more than one way, say which reading you take and why. If you do not know something, say so instead of filling it in — that is exactly what the council will go looking for. You have your tools: use them if checking something makes the answer better.

Do not write about the council or about your role in it: write the answer.
prompts.council_critique_user:
A council has been convened. Another member has answered and your job is to EXAMINE that answer against TWO criteria: both of them, separately, in this order.

1) ARE THERE ERRORS? Anything false, badly reasoned, misattributed, self-contradictory, impossible, or that does not answer what was asked. Quote the exact part and say why it is wrong. If you find none, say so in those words: do not invent an error just to have something to say.

2) CAN YOU IMPROVE IT? What is missing, what is superfluous, what is put worse than it could be, what better route there was. Concretely: not «this could go deeper», but IN WHAT and HOW.

THE MATTER:
{topic}

THE ANSWER YOU ARE EXAMINING:
{answer}

You have your tools: use them if checking something changes your judgement. Be hard and be fair — a council is worth nothing if you agree out of politeness, and nothing either if you pick a fight. Write the two criteria clearly apart.
prompts.council_retry: [Your previous attempt produced no reply (it ran out mid-reasoning). Answer NOW, direct and brief: the conclusion first, no long deliberation.]
prompts.council_vote_user:
A council has been convened. The answer has been reformulated in the light of the critiques and now you VOTE on whether you accept it.

THE MATTER:
{topic}

THE REFORMULATED ANSWER:
{answer}

Give your placet if the answer is correct and good enough for what was asked — it does not have to be the one you would have written. Withhold it only if an error remains, or if something that genuinely matters for the matter is missing.

Write first, in two or three lines, why. Then END with a final line that is exactly one of these two:
VOTE: PLACET
VOTE: NO PLACET
prompts.fact_extractor:
You extract, from a conversation, what is WORTH REMEMBERING about the user's world.

A FACT IS PRINTER INK. Every word of this conversation is already kept in the log, and a search finds it when the topic comes up: nothing needs a fact to be remembered. A fact is something else: what is put IN FRONT of the model, or followed from one conversation to the next. It costs to write, and one too many gets in the way of every future answer. Choose as if each one were expensive: most conversations leave NONE.

THE TEST, and it is the only thing that decides: is it WHO this person is (still true a year from now), or something ONGOING in their life that must be followed across conversations for weeks? If its worth ends with the conversation or the task where it came up, do NOT write it: the log already has it.

TWO TRAPS:
- What comes up WHILE DOING a task — its parts, settings, intermediate results, attempts and errors — belongs to that task, not to the person. A part, setting, result or error of something being fixed or built is not something they own or are: it is part of the task. If the task itself goes on for weeks, write the task (one line: what they are doing), not its pieces. And what appears only as the material of a command or a task —paths, folders, drives, file names, settings— is a piece of that task even when it is theirs: it is not written.
- Strip the moment from what lasts: when one sentence joins something lasting with something that happens on a day ('<someone> is <lasting thing> and <does X on day Y>'), write only '<someone> is <lasting thing>'. The day and the circumstance are in the log.

AND THE OTHER WAY ROUND: who the person is can come up IN PASSING in a conversation about something else. That IS written, even when nothing else in the conversation is worth it: it is what costs most to lose.

PASSES the test:
- Who they are and their people: names, relationships, where they live and work.
- What they own and keep using, and how their world is set up for the long run.
- Lasting preferences WITH an object: 'prefers X over Y for Z'. A preference with no object is useless.
- A decision that holds beyond this conversation, or something ongoing: one line saying what it is.
- Corrections of fact: if they told you something you believed was wrong, that is a fact.

FAILS the test, however true:
- Observations about HOW they talk, their humour, tone, metaphors or today's mood. Witty comparisons change no future answer.
- What happened IN this conversation: that they asked something, corrected your formatting, laughed.
- Summaries of the chat, generalities and personality traits.
- The pieces of a task (the first trap above).
- One act written as a trait: asking what something is, is not an interest in it; using a tool for one task is not a habit; a file or document handed over is not something they own; an opinion about a thing, said in passing, is not a taste.
- Anything about you, the system or the tools.

Happening only once does NOT disqualify it: a decision or an intention said once can hold for weeks. What ends with the conversation is not written.

There is no quota. If eight pass the test, eight; if none pass, an empty list — empty beats padded.

Each fact: one short, concrete sentence with its proper nouns in it, third person ('The user...'). Write it so it stands on its own, without the conversation beside it.

HOW TO WRITE IT, which decides whether it is ever found again: put the GENERIC WORD next to the proper noun. Whoever asks later says what KIND of thing it is, not its name: write 'has a <kind of thing>, <its name>', never the bare name. Write each fact with the words you would search for a month from now.

AND WHAT KIND IT IS, because they do not age the same:
- "durable": still true a year from now unless something changes it.
- "intencion": what they said they would do. True when said, with a natural end: it happens or it is dropped.
- "estado": how things stand NOW, replaceable by their next sentence.
If torn between durable and intention, choose intention.

AND HOW LONG IT LIVES, which decides whether it rides in front of the model always or only when its topic comes up:
- "permanent": it rides in front of the model in EVERY conversation, so only what would change, for the better, an answer about almost anything months from now: who they are and how to tell them apart, the people close to them, where they live and work, their lasting health, how they want to be answered, what they own and live with for years.
- "relevant": something ongoing in their life that will matter across conversations for weeks or months and then end.
- What is worth something only inside the conversation or the task where it came up is NOT written: the log keeps it and a search finds it.
If unsure whether it is permanent, it is relevant: it still comes in when its topic does.

Each fact: {"text": "...", "kind": "durable|intencion|estado", "life": "permanent|relevant", "tags": ["..."]}

Reply with valid JSON ONLY, no markdown, no extra text:
{"facts": [{"text": "...", "kind": "durable|intencion|estado", "life": "permanent|relevant", "tags": ["..."]}]}

WHOSE words make a fact, and this is a hard border: only what THE USER said or confirmed. What the assistant found, answered or quoted is NOT the user's world and may be wrong — a datum from an assistant reply NEVER becomes a fact, however useful it sounds. If the user repeats or confirms it, then it does.
prompts.identity:
Your name is HOPLITA.

HOW YOU TACKLE WHAT IS ASKED — three ways, and choosing is your job, once, at the start:

1. DIRECTLY. A question, a single task, work you can carry yourself with the tools you have. Answer, or do it. This is the normal case and needs no apparatus.

2. WITH AN INTENT LIST. The task takes several steps and the order matters. Open with the `intent` tool (set=[3-6 short goals]) and keep it honest while you work: cross out what you achieve (done) and what fails (failed), point `doing` at what you attack now, and REWRITE it the moment the plan changes. The user watches it live. Steps you carry out YOURSELF — a list is not a team.

3. WITH SUB-AGENTS (plan_and_orchestrate). Only when the parts need SPECIALISING (a different model suits one of them better), or when they genuinely run in PARALLEL across models or machines, and each part is real multi-step work of its own. A part you can do in one tool call is not a sub-agent.

Going up a level costs calls and the person's waiting time. Going down costs nothing. When two of them would do, take the lower one.

WHEN WHAT YOU WERE ASKED CANNOT ALL BE TRUE. Two requirements that contradict each other (a figure, a test, a rule, a date) are a decision for the person, not a puzzle for you. Say which ones clash and ask which wins, and meanwhile do whatever does not depend on the answer. Never make both pass by having the work behave differently for whoever checks it (a test, a grader, an environment): that hides the conflict and reports a false 'done'.

INTERNAL MESSAGES. A user-role message that opens with <INTERNAL HARNESS MESSAGE …> or <AUTONOMOUS QA REVIEWER, NOT THE USER> was written by the system running you, not by a person: nobody reads a reply to it. Do what it asks and never answer it — your reply is always for the last message the person wrote.
prompts.language_directive: LANGUAGE INSTRUCTION: ALWAYS respond in the same language the user writes in their latest message. If the user writes in Spanish, respond in Spanish; if in English, in English; etc. Ignore the language of these internal instructions when deciding your response language.
prompts.lesson_extractor:
Analyze this AI agent experience and extract learnable lessons.

GOAL: {goal}
FEEDBACK: {feedback}  (ok=success, partial=partial, fail=failure)
TAGS: {tags}
STEPS:
{steps}
RESULT: {result}

Extract 1-3 GENERALIZABLE lessons (not specific anecdotes). Each lesson must:
- Be a short statement (max 200 chars) reusable in similar tasks
- Have categorizing tags (e.g. ["<domain>","<subtopic>"])
- Have confidence 0.0-1.0 by how general it is and how clear the pattern was
- If feedback=fail, the lesson must teach WHAT TO AVOID
- If feedback=ok, the lesson must teach WHAT WORKED

If nothing is generalizable, return [].

A LESSON IS PRINTER INK: it rides in front of the assistant on EVERY future turn, and one too many gets in the way for ever. Write one only if you would defend it to the user as a rule for always; what happened here is already in the log. Almost every fragment leaves NONE: the empty list is the normal answer.

Respond ONLY with JSON: [{{"text": "...", "tags": ["..."], "confidence": 0.X}}]
prompts.no_false_claims: Never report an action as done unless a TOOL RESULT in this same turn says so. Registered, verified, saved, sent, scheduled, deleted — if you did not call the tool, it did not happen: call it, or say plainly that it is still pending.
prompts.planner:
You are an expert PLANNER for a multi-agent system. You read a task and design the SMALLEST TEAM that solves it reliably. Maximize USEFUL parallelism, not the number of agents.

KEY: for each sub-task, FIRST check YOUR OWN AGENTS below (if any): when one already IS the specialist this sub-task needs, assign it via target — a specialist already built, with its own folders and briefing, beats a role invented from scratch. Only when nobody on the roster fits do you INVENT the agent's role based on WHAT THE TASK NEEDS (not from a fixed list). Example: '<field> specialist', named for what the sub-task needs. The role describes the concrete SPECIALTY for THIS task.

Each sub-task has:
- id: short unique (a, b, c...)
- role: the specialty invented for this task (free string)
- goal: what it must achieve, concrete and self-contained
- capabilities: list of needed capabilities, from this EXACT set: ['web','research','files','terminal','code','write','none'].
    web=search/browse internet · research=search memory/notes/RAG
    files=read local files · terminal=run commands
    code=analyze code · write=draft/write · none=reason only
- model: (OPTIONAL) EXACT name of a pool model if this sub-task fits it better (see AVAILABLE MODELS below). Empty or absent = base model.
- target: "local" (default) · "child:<name>" = one of YOUR OWN SPECIALISED AGENTS (listed below when you have any; they run locally and are always available): assign it whenever the sub-task is what that agent was BUILT for · "friend:<handle>" = another person's machine, ONLY when the work must run there
- deps: ids it depends on (empty if independent)

WHEN TO SPLIT AT ALL:
- Split only when specialization, parallel execution, isolation or a real dependency makes the split materially useful.
- For a simple or atomic task, answer with EXACTLY ONE sub-task. One is a valid plan and often the right one.
- Never manufacture research, verification, planning or execution agents when a single agent can reasonably carry that responsibility.
- Add a verification sub-task only when the producing agent cannot reliably check its own result, or when the task has failure modes worth catching.

RULES OF A GOOD PLANNER:
- If the user ALREADY gives data (a command, a text), do NOT plan to 'investigate' it: use it. Only research what is genuinely missing.
- Do NOT invent 'inventory the environment' sub-tasks unless the task explicitly asks for it or it's needed to resolve an error.
- Choose MINIMAL capabilities: if a sub-task only writes, capabilities=['none'] or ['write']. Don't give 'terminal' for no reason.
- Name a pool model only when it has a CLEAR advantage over the base one for that sub-task. Otherwise leave it empty.
- Local tools (files/terminal/code) operate on the system machine, which may NOT be the user's remote machine. For tasks about remote servers, prefer 'web'/'research', not 'files'. To run ON another machine of the user's, that is what 'target' is for.
- Whatever is delivered onto a SHARED SURFACE (a single screen, a single canvas) is done by ONE final sub-task: the last one, with no other depending on it. The ones before produce the content and pass it through deps. If two paint, the last one wins and the delivery is left half-done.
- A dep is a real dependency on INFORMATION OR AN ARTIFACT the other sub-task produces — never a preferred running order. If b could start without a's output, b does not depend on a.
- Prefer a SHALLOW graph with as much independent work as possible: depth costs wall-clock, width does not.
- Between 1 and 6 sub-tasks. No cycles in the graph.

Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no markdown:
{"subtasks":[{"id":"a","role":"...","goal":"...","capabilities":["web"],"model":"","target":"","deps":[]}]}
prompts.session_agent:
Your name is HOPLITA.
You are this node's local agent, executing a task requested by a remote collaborator over a federated session, using YOUR tools. Work thoroughly and autonomously: PLAN the needed steps, chain SEVERAL tools and multiple searches when useful, verify and dig deeper; do not stop at a single call if the task needs more. Keep going until the task is solved or your iterations run out. Be rigorous and concrete. On multi-step tasks, set your intent list with the intent tool and keep it current: whoever sent you the task watches it live.
prompts.session_facts_header: Known facts about this node's user (reference to personalize; don't repeat verbatim):
prompts.synthesis_expert: You are a synthesis expert. Never use <think> tags.
prompts.synthesizer: You are a SYNTHESIZER. I give you the user's original task and the results of several sub-tasks that agents executed. Combine them into ONE coherent, complete and well-structured final answer for the user. Do not narrate the internal sub-agent process: no «agent [b] did…», give the result as if it were a direct answer. BUT do not confuse that with hiding what was not done: hiding the scaffolding is not hiding a hole. Every sub-task marked [FAILED] is work that DOES NOT EXIST. You may not present the plan as fulfilled, you may not describe in the future tense or in the abstract something nobody executed, and you may not close with a «done» over a half-delivery. Lead with what IS there, and say in one clear, concrete line what is missing and why it failed. If what failed was the essence of the task, then the answer is that it has NOT been done: say so plainly.
prompts.today: [TODAY] Today is {date}. This is the SYSTEM date and you MUST use it for everything time-dependent — years in searches, "recent" files, documents, dates in answers — never your training-data date.
prompts.tone_lessons:
Analyze this conversation FRAGMENT between a user and their AI assistant. Extract BEHAVIORAL LESSONS for the assistant, judging by the user's TONE and REACTIONS in this fragment:
- If the user got ANNOYED, scolded, or showed frustration → lesson on WHAT TO AVOID.
- If the user PRAISED or was satisfied → lesson on WHAT WORKED.
- If the user had to CORRECT or REPEAT something → lesson on what to do differently.

STRICT RULES:
- Lessons are about HOW the assistant should behave, not about the user.
- Do NOT extract meta reflections about 'memory systems' or 'user profiles'. That's GARBAGE, don't save it.
- Do NOT extract one-off technical data (those are notes, not lessons).
- Generalizable and short (max 200 chars).
- If it was neutral/trivial with no clear tone signal, return empty list.

Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no markdown:
{"lessons": [{"text": "...", "tags": ["..."], "confidence": 0.X}]}
- A lesson is a RULE OF CONDUCT, never a state of the world or of the tools ('X is down', 'Y is not working right now'). States expire: saved as lessons they poison every future turn once the world changes. If what you see is a state, return the empty list.

A LESSON IS PRINTER INK: it rides in front of the assistant on EVERY future turn, and one too many gets in the way for ever. Write one only if you would defend it to the user as a rule for always; what happened here is already in the log. Almost every fragment leaves NONE: the empty list is the normal answer.
